questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A big motivation for me going on exchange was to meet a ton of people with different backgrounds and nationalities. The oppurtunity to put myself in a situation that would force me to seek out new friendships in a foreign setting, seemed like a fantastic way to grow as a person. Since it can be incredibly demanding to venture out on your own to study for a semester, my goal was to find a highly international country but with a culture that is not too different from my own.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange stay was interesting and exciting but I unfortunately did not get all the courses that I had wished for and my housing was located too far from campus. This resulted in me having to spend a lot of time commuting and studying subjects that I found incredibly challenging.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very straight forward. All the information that I need was sent by mail in due time. Whenever I had a question for either my home or host university, they would quickly reply to my mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My host university had arranged a Welcome Week with various informative events. It all began with a welcome show that was composed of a concert by students and an informational presentation by the International Office at Utrecht University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was quite challenging and I eventually ended up contacting an agent. For the price of one month's rent, the agent quickly found me a place in Haarlem.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would urge anybody to prioritize finding a place as close to campus as possible. Most of the social activities happen around campus or inside the city of Utrecht. Having to commute for almost 2 hours each direction makes it hard to attend events happening in the evening.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All I had to do was specify my first and second priorities for each block of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The instructions for the registration were clear and when I after one lecture contacted the administration because I could tell I did not meet the prerequisites for a course, they were kind and immediately transferred me to another.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I unfortunately did not end up getting my preffered courses but like I described in the prevoius question, they were very helpful and transfered me from one course to another after I requested it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to double check the prerequisites. I officially met the prerequisites based on courses that I had completed, but I still did not possess the proficiency needed to participate in one of the courses. I identified this after the first lecture and luckily got transferred to another course that I really enjoyed. 

Another point to make is that some courses will have prerequisites that you do not officially comply with. If you are confident that you have the neccesary knowledge to participate in some of those courses anyway, it is well worth your time to describe the situation. I ended up not getting some of my first priorities because I did not meet the prerequisites based on courses completed. If I had explained that I had adeqate knowledge of the subject anyway, I might have ended up participating in the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only participated in BA courses. The academic level was comparable to that of UCPH's courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the exact same style and structure of teaching. Each course was composed of lectures and exercise classes. During the exercise classes we would work individually or in groups on exercises related to the lecture that had happened beforehand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Image Processing
- Data Analytics
- Intro to Machine Learning
- Functional Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly reccomend Data Analytics and Image Processing.
The proffesor who is in charge of the Data Analytics course is extremely passionate about teaching, which made me look forward to every
lecture.The
assignemnts were small hands on projects with real data and I always felt motivated to work on them.
I especially liked Image Processing because of the assignments. Each assignment had us implement different image processing functions that we got to apply images. In addition to these assignments being exciting, they also strengthened my coding skills.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up paying a lot of money for public transportation. This was a natural consequence of finding housing far from campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: All my expenses were similar to the ones I have in Denmark except for the price of public transportation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very common for dutch students to be members of student associations. There are both student associations based on study programme and student associations based on hobbies. I ended up signing up for a general student association that hosted a weekly event every Tuesday. This was a great way to ensure that I socialised with people outside of class.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a student association that focuses on a hobby or a more general one were the focus is being social and where the activities differ from week to week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The number one priority after getting settled in your hosuing situation should be to aquire a bike. A bike will enable your to get around Utrecht faster and much cheaper than any other method. Utrecht is a lovely city to spend your weekends hanging out in. 

The Netherlands has a lot of stunning and charming old cities and since the public transportation network is well structured and effective, you can easily visit a new wonderful city every week.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture in the Netherlands is very simlar to that of Denmark's.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most local students are already a part of "estabilshed" friend groups and thus it can be intimidating to approach them. Using group projects as opportunities to get to know people and potentially befriend them, I found to be a good idea.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any cultural differences when it comes to behaviour but I generally found the cities to be more chaotic, more lively and less clean.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the Dutch market culture. Twice a week I would bike to a market in Haarlem (the city I lived in) to buy a bite to eat or a bouquet of flowers to bring home to my appartment. The weekly markets where always buzling with people and they always gave me a wonderful sensation of being in some medieval marketplace.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Make sure that find courses that you are passionate about and do what you can to guarantee that you get them.
2) Find housing as close to the campus or Utrecht city as possible. 
3) Sign up for a student association.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The housing crisis in the Netherlands is very severe. Make sure to start looking for housing early.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange stay was getting to meet curious and ambitious people from all around the world who had come to Utrecht to widen their horizons and meet new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was living way too far away from Utrecht which made it incredibly hard for me to find the time and energy to participate in social activities happening in Utrecht.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
